newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical excluded from Vancouver case.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical excluded from Vancouver case.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co on Thursday said a judge in Vancouver had ruled that a class-action suit related to breast implants would exclude the company.

According to a order, made with the consent of the attorneys for both sides, Dow Chemical will not be included in a class action certified in the Canadian province of British Columbia on the question of whether breast implants are fit for their intended purpose.

Dow Chemical has said it never designed, manufactured or tested breast implants. The devices were manufactured by Dow Corning Corp, in which each Dow Chemical and Corning Inc are 50 percent shareholders.

In April 1996, British Columbia Supreme Court Justice Kenneth Mackenzie granted class-action status to a case brought on behalf of about 1,000 women by a Vancouver-area woman who claimed to have been injured by the devices. The women claim they have suffered a variety of ailments because of the silicone-gel breast implants.

At that time, Mackenzie said the status of Dow Chemical would have to be decided at a later time. Dow Chemical had contended it should not be part of the action and claimed it was named in the case only because of its ownership in Dow Corning.
The consent order also left open the option for Dow Chemical to move for dismissal from the pending class proceedings in British Columbia.
"We will move for dismissal. We haven't decided when we will do that," said Marsha Rabiteau, a Dow Chemical attorney on a conference call with reporters.
Both sides claimed victory after the order.

"Justice Mackenzie's order is a significant victory for Dow Chemical. It means Dow Chemical is not part of the class certified in British Columbia," said Dow Chemical General Counsel John Scriven, in a statement.

David Klein, a Vancouver-based attorney for the plaintiffs, said, that while Dow Chemical was excluded from this certification, "We are free to apply to the court to certify the case against Dow Chemical on the secondary question of whether Dow Chemical is liable for the negligence of Dow Corning,...or any secondary issue."
"It was really important for Dow to remain in the suit, and we achieved that today," Klein told Reuters in a telephone interview from his offices in Vancouver.
